correctness.rationale: For arbitrary m≥1 and S, forward chain forces identical reachability. All allowed 2paths are chain–chain, chain–chord, chord–chain, with distinct missing endpoint pairs; projection of boundaries onto forbidden arrows is injective, giving Omega2=0 over Z. The chain-spanning-tree incidence kernel has primitive explicit basis z_ab for each chord, hence H1=Z^|S|. Complete subsets yield each k≤m². Reproducibility checker passed 725 finite instances; the infinite result uses proof, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: Muranov–Muranova newly associate Alexandrov path topologies to concatenating digraph path complexes, inviting an exact test of their information loss. The theorem shows that even a fixed labeled T0 total order admits every integral first-path Betti rank in an interval growing quadratically in vertex count, with explicit primitive cycles. This separates the full quantitative first-homology information from the most rigid reachability topology and matches the ambient O(n²) growth rate. It is more than a single negative example, while not asserting the global sharp constant.
